# Independent review: the PR552 complex bad-class surcharge

**Assessment: removal is justified under the same inherited exact complex-cover/compiler assumptions.** This review supports omitting the additional bad-residue fallback from the complex recurrence only. It does not certify a numerical improvement, weaken the bit recurrence, or discharge any inherited all-size theorem.

## Original recurrence distinction

The pinned `notes/three-stage-cover-assembly.tex` at commit12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b gives the complex moment as the exact child-profile sum, divided by the complex live stock. It then separately introduces the entire32*m_b^2-child fallback on a10^-16 fraction of every ideal edge of the **bit** ledger. Its precision/router guard explicitly retains the full finite orthogonal group and Clifford routers.

The adjacent pinned `notes/general-clifford-frames.tex` constructs exact Gaussian-dyadic representatives for every binary subspace, exact nested transitions, rank-zero adapters, and dirty-tail/reverse identities. It gives exact algebraic operators, not good-class operators accompanied by a failed residue-class fraction. Fixed binary GL matrices that choose these representatives are invertible address maps over F2; they are not the q-adic selectors responsible for bit-side fallback.

Both original note hashes and Git-blob identities were independently checked against the parent acquisition pins; see REVIEW.json.

## Actual PR552 compiler audit

This conclusion follows from the emitted program and its exact controller, not merely from an absence of keywords:

1. `emit_local.py` emits both orientations from the selected source. Every positive-rank frame climb and center descent is explicitly a recursive child; all scalar operations, coefficient work, phases, and residual adapters remain separate finite work. It checks all exact scalar columns and paid-profile equality.
2. `emit_supplier_hosted.py` assigns each entire helper invocation to an explicit physical family and orthogonal chart. Its profile is the sum over all72 complete local invocations plus every nonempty idle remainder. The emitted asynchronous schedule retains every source event on each replica and the final correction.
3. `audit_supplier_hosted.py` independently checks all owner windows, one-owner exclusivity, residual/spectator axes, phase bindings, and every explicit remainder. It reconstructs actual orthogonal73-column charts and the same global histogram. It rejects omitted idle children and invalid owner assignments.
4. `invoice_final.py` recounts all scalar/Horner work, wrappers, adapters, movement, and router costs. It charges the full finite orthogonal group and preserves the precision, tape, external-row and halving guards. Its prefix argument uses exact right-translation bijections on the cover group, so every cover vertex obeys the same operator construction.

The prior independent physical replay receipts have been checked for PASS and matching template/owner hashes. This review does not rerun that full physical verifier. The actual2,972 owner-chart types are finitely checked; the enormous entire orthogonal group is not enumerated element-by-element. The translation-bijection argument supplies the uniform passage to the full cover.

Consequently the complex controller has an exact exhaustive recursive-child profile. There is no further width-dependent good/bad q-adic selector in this construction requiring a fraction of additional recursive fallback children. The finite Clifford routers and adapters are already paid in the unchanged finite invoice. Removing them, or removing other precision/row guards, would not follow from this argument.

## Where the extra term enters

`vendor535/code/assemble_combined.py` uses one generic `two_moments` function for both suppliers. It calls the moment engine with `bad=True` and explicitly adds the fallback through the second engine for the complex profile as well as the bit profile. The original moment engine labels that option an inherited envelope and makes the default `bad=False`. Thus the correction is a recurrence-model choice at assembly, not a changed scalar word, owner schedule, or hidden physical optimization.

For complex profile H, dimension m, and live stock W, retain exactly

    sum_r H[r] * (r/m)^(1-b) / W.

Omit only the additional complex term proportional to32*m^2*sum(H)/10^16. Keep the entire bit bad-class surcharge and all its mutable-source/selector assumptions.

## Scope and relation to PR557

This remains conditional on the retained all-size realization, common-label/compiler, completed-call hosting, semantic precision, fixed-tape/exact-recovery, and analytic-transfer interfaces. The review does not replace these assumptions with a new theorem. Under those same interfaces, a uniform exact complex cover uses its pure child moment, matching the original complex assembly argument. A port to a different complex implementation that actually has exceptional residue classes would require its own analysis.

PR557 explicitly fixes its conservative bad-class charge and excludes alternative charges from its ceiling. Changing that unnecessary complex surcharge therefore lies outside that certificate's stated model; it does not contradict the verified fixed-charge ceiling. Separately, PR557 fixes the PR551 scalar word and does not directly cover final PR552.

No numerical value is claimed by this review. Both rational engines, the next endpoint, all strict outer inequalities, and a publication package must be checked by the parent before announcing a new conditional bound. No PR or provider source was edited, and all artifacts remain on the mounted SSD.
